cases.state: seeded fixture, plus a redirector EVAL Rule Set (default https://eval-ruleset-default.example/) whose only rule, EVAL Catch-all, sends every visitor to https://eval-catchall.example/; setup gives it a tracker (link in /tmp/p202-eval-ruleset.url) and writes the catch-all's id to /tmp/p202-eval-ruleset.catchall
setup: r=$(p202 rotator list --all --json | jq -r '[.data[] | select(.name=="EVAL Rule Set")][0].id // empty') && { [ -n "$r" ] || r=$(p202 rotator create --name 'EVAL Rule Set' --default-url https://eval-ruleset-default.example/ --json | jq -r '.data.id'); } && echo "$r" > /tmp/p202-eval-ruleset.id && test -s /tmp/p202-eval-ruleset.id

r=$(cat /tmp/p202-eval-ruleset.id) && c=$(p202 campaign list --all --json | jq -r '[.data[] | select(.aff_campaign_name=="EVAL Campaign A")][0].aff_campaign_id') && t=$(p202 tracker list --all --json | jq -r --arg r "$r" '[.data[] | select((.rotator_id|tostring)==$r)][0].tracker_id // empty') && { [ -n "$t" ] || t=$(p202 tracker create --aff-campaign-id "$c" --rotator-id "$r" --json | jq -r '.data.tracker_id'); } && p202 tracker get-url "$t" --json | jq -r '.data.direct_url' > /tmp/p202-eval-ruleset.url && test -s /tmp/p202-eval-ruleset.url
cases.ask: On the EVAL Rule Set redirector, split visitors from 203.0.113.60 evenly between https://eval-split-a.example/ and https://eval-split-b.example/. That has to be tried before the catch-all rule already there, which should keep sending everyone else where it does now.

checks.run: u=$(cat /tmp/p202-eval-ruleset.url); for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}\n' -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.60' "$u"; done | sed -E 's#^https?://([^/]+).*#\1#' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' '

p202 rotator get "$(cat /tmp/p202-eval-ruleset.id)" --json | jq --arg kept "$(cat /tmp/p202-eval-ruleset.catchall)" '.data.rules | length == 2 and .[0].splittest == 1 and ([.[0].redirects[].weight | tonumber] | length == 2 and .[0] == .[1] and .[0] > 0) and (.[1].id | tostring) == $kept'

expected.rubric: PASS if clicks from 203.0.113.60 now split between the two URLs at equal weights, the catch-all rule is the same rule as before (its id unchanged) and still second, so everyone else still reaches https://eval-catchall.example/, and the reply says so. FAIL if the new rule sits after the catch-all (where it never matches), the catch-all is removed, re-made or changed, or the agent reports success with the rule not in place.

cases.notes: The redirects try the rules in their set's order and the first that matches sends the visitor. A rule added on its own (rule-create) goes after the catch-all, which then takes every visitor, so the new rule only works ahead of it: PUT /rotators/{id}/rules (`p202 rotator set-rules`, rotator_set_rules) puts it there and keeps the catch-all's id, so its clicks stay its own. The first check fires 20 real clicks through rtr.php (both URLs appear unless one weight is 0, with odds 2 in a million); the third holds the order, the equal weights and the kept id.

cases.ask: What would change if the EVAL Rule Set redirector sent visitors from 203.0.113.62 to https://eval-preview.example/ ahead of its catch-all rule? Show me the change, but don't make it yet.

expected.rubric: PASS if the agent previews the new set with a dry run, reports that a rule for 203.0.113.62 would be added ahead of the catch-all (which would be kept), and the redirector is unchanged afterwards. FAIL if the rule set changes, a proposal is staged, or the agent describes a change it did not preview.

cases.notes: The negative twin of rotator-rules-001: `p202 rotator set-rules <id> --dry-run` (rotator_set_rules with dry_run: true) answers the set as it would be stored and each rule's change, and writes nothing. The click check proves the redirect still sends 203.0.113.62 to the catch-all.
